transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Leah Thompson (Aurum Legal), Marco Reyes (Aurum Procurement), Samir Patel (Aurum CTO)

Summary (auto-generated): quick procurement and legal check — review MSA/DPA and SLA appendix, discuss pricing & PO, align on onboarding steps and benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey all, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call — Jordan Meyers, AE, Redwood; Priya Shah, solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya: Hi everyone.
[00:10] Leah: Leah Thompson here, head of legal at Aurum.
[00:12] Marco: Marco Reyes, procurement.
[00:14] Samir: Samir Patel, CTO. Sorry I'm a few minutes late, running between calls.
[00:20] Jordan: No problem at all. Agenda — go through the redlines you sent on the MSA and DPA, walk the SLA appendix and pricing buckets, then confirm next steps for procurement and onboarding. Sound good?
[00:28] Leah: Yep, good. I'll probably jump in on the legal points.
[00:31] Marco: We'll want to lock timeline, PO process, and any payment milestones.
[00:35] Priya: I'll cover technical questions on hosting options, encryption, and benchmarks.

[02:00] Leah: On the MSA, our main asks are around liability caps — we'd like to see a mutual cap tied to fees paid over 12 months, and clearer breach notification timelines. Also indemnities — we have standard carve-outs for third-party data. I saw Redwood's standard is 12 months of fees, can you confirm?
[02:18] Jordan: Sure, our standard cap is twelve months of fees for hosted customers; for enterprise/dedicated deals we can discuss higher caps or a hybrid approach. We can be flexible depending on the commit and also on insurance proof.
[02:30] Leah: Okay, would you accept a mutual cap instead of Redwood-only?
[02:34] Jordan: We typically do mutual for larger deals. I'll put that into our proposed redline.
[02:39] Leah: Great. On breach notif — we usually ask for 72 hours for confirmed incidents, with updates. Your DPA mentions 'reasonable efforts' which is a bit vague.
[02:49] Priya: Yeah, on the DPA we have a set timeline we publish in our security pack — usually initial ack within 48 hours and more detailed updates within 72. We'll make the DPA language more prescriptive in the redline.

[04:10] Marco: On data residency — Aurum has EU customers and we'd like EU data residency for embeddings and logs. Can Redwood guarantee that for Hosted? Or do we need Dedicated?
[04:20] Priya: For hosted, we do regional processing in our EU region and can route EU traffic to EU-only infra, but full contractual data residency guarantees typically come with Dedicated or Private deployments. For strict residency and isolation, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[04:36] Samir: If we do Dedicated, what's the timeline to provision? Procurement needs to know lead time.
[04:41] Jordan: For Dedicated reserved pools, typical ramp is 6-8 weeks once contracts and payment are in place, sometimes faster depending on capacity and GPU type. We can start a pilot on hosted in parallel while Dedicated is provisioned to avoid blocking.

[06:05] Leah: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? We need BYOK and proof of no-key access by Redwood.
[06:14] Priya: Yes, we support KMS integrations; HSM for Private deployments. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and we can supply attestation that keys are not accessible by our team. We'll include vendor-specific notes in the security pack.

[08:00] Marco: Pricing — the numbers in the SOW are high level. Procurement will need the price schedule and any volume discounts. Also do you invoice monthly or net 30 after invoice?
[08:12] Jordan: Standard is monthly invoicing with Net-30 payment terms, though we can do Net-45 for new enterprise accounts if needed. Volume discounts apply at committed monthly token thresholds; we'll send a detailed price schedule.

[09:40] Leah: SLA — your SLA mentions 99.9% availability for hosted and higher for Dedicated? Can you clarify the latency SLOs and credits?
[09:50] Priya: Right, hosted is 99.9% uptime SLO for API availability on regional endpoints; Dedicated has tiered SLOs (e.g., 99.95 or 99.99 depending on configuration and reserved commit). For latency, we provide percentile-based latency targets in the SLA appendix (p95/p99) for typical request profiles — we'll share the benchmark attachment. Credits are proportional to downtime and have caps in the SLA tier; these are standard service credit calculations.
[10:25] Samir: For our latency-sensitive flows we need p95 < 120ms for chat paths with seq len ~512. Do you have examples where that is achievable on hosted?
[10:36] Priya: For chat at 512, depending on model choice and region, p95 can be under 120ms on Dedicated with optimized GPUs; hosted can hit close to that for smaller models. We'll include our internal benchmark sheet with model/config examples to show expected p95 numbers. Keep in mind network variability and KV cache warming affect first requests.

[12:05] Marco: Procurement note — we need to get pricing approval by May 6 to align with budget cycle. If Redwood can provide the redlined MSA, DPA, price schedule, and invoice terms by next Friday we can route for internal approval.
[12:18] Jordan: Understood — we'll target delivering that.

[13:45] Leah: A couple more legal items: audit rights — we ask for SOC2 Type II or an annual audit report; also subprocessor list and notification for changes.
[13:55] Priya: We are SOC2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. Subprocessor list is maintained and we notify customers of material changes; we'll include the most recent list in the security pack.

[15:30] Marco: PO process — do you accept a PO up front? Any minimum invoice?
[15:36] Jordan: Yes, we accept POs; for onboarding for Dedicated we generally require a first invoice upfront or a short-term deposit tied to provisioning costs for GPUs. We'll flag that in the SOW options.

[17:00] Samir: On data retention — embeddings and logs — what's default retention and can we shorten it? We want embeddings purged after 30 days unless explicitly retained.
[17:10] Priya: Default retention is 90 days for logs, embeddings retention depends on product — for Redwood-hosted embeddings we can set retention window by contract; 30 days is feasible. We'll include retention controls in the DPA appendix.

[19:00] Leah: Liability for model outputs — we need indemnities around third-party claims for generated content, particularly for regulated verticals. How does Redwood handle that?
[19:11] Jordan: We have standard indemnity language; for high-risk use cases we recommend model governance and evals; we can add clarifying language about misuse and our safe-guarding measures. Full carve-outs for customer-controlled prompts are typical. We'll propose language that balances both sides.

[22:40] Marco: One operational question — do you provide detailed monthly usage reports, token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback?
[22:48] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards and we can export CSVs for cost allocation. We also provide tracing hooks for latency analysis.

[24:15] Leah: On data subject requests and privacy — how quickly can you support a DSAR? 30 days?
[24:22] Priya: We follow standard 30-day windows; for Hosted we can perform searches and exports as per the DPA obligations. We'll include playbook steps in the security pack.

[26:00] Samir: Technical question — for Dedicated, can we bring our own model weights or must we use Redwood-curated models? We have some fine-tuned models we want to serve.
[26:10] Priya: Dedicated and Private support customer-provided weights with some caveats around licensing and compatibility. We'll need to validate model format and do onboarding testing; performance tuning may be required. We'll add this to the POC scoping if you want to validate latency and throughput.

[28:40] Marco: Good. I'd like to confirm the documents one more time: redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2, price schedule, SLA appendix, and onboarding checklist. If those arrive next week procurement can push approval.
[28:52] Jordan: We'll prioritize that.

[30:00] Leah: A small note — we'd like an explicit clause for data deletion upon contract termination and confirmation of destruction certificate.
[30:08] Priya: Yes, we can include a data destruction certificate clause and a process for evidence of deletion.

[32:15] Marco: For signatures, do you have an e-sign vendor preference? DocuSign OK?
[32:20] Jordan: DocuSign is fine.

[33:40] Samir: One more item — is there a vendor security questionnaire we can fill out? We're going to run this through our security tooling.
[33:47] Priya: Yes, we have a security questionnaire (we can provide in XLS) plus our security pack. I'll send the pack and the current questionnaire answers.

[35:50] Jordan: Okay recap — Jordan will send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing schedule, Priya will share security pack, SOC2 report under NDA and the SLA appendix with benchmarks, Marco will route for procurement timeline. Proposed dates? We said next Friday for documents, May 6 for procurement approval.
[36:08] Marco: That's right.
[36:15] Leah: Sounds good. One ask — can you call out any escalation contacts and SRE on-call info in the SLA appendix?
[36:22] Priya: We'll include escalation matrix and on-call response time commitments in the appendix.

[38:00] Jordan: Any blockers from anyone?
[38:04] Leah: Not if you provide the redlines as discussed.
[38:07] Marco: No blockers.
[38:10] Samir: Nope.

[40:00] Jordan: Great, we'll get those docs to you. We'll also propose a technical onboarding slot for April 29 for Priya to run an infra walkthrough and a pilot plan.
[40:10] Marco: Works for me.
[40:15] Leah: Works.
[40:20] Priya: I'll send calendar invite after the redlines go out.

[42:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package and next steps.
[42:06] Leah: Thank you.
[42:09] Marco: Thanks.
[42:11] Samir: Thanks all.

[44:00] (call ends)

Notes/Artifacts referenced: link: Redlined MSA (TBD); link: Redwood security pack (to be sent); link: SLA appendix + benchmarks (to be sent); price schedule spreadsheet (to be sent).

Call end recap (auto): Deliver MSA/DPA redlines, SLA appendix with benchmarks, SOC2 & security pack under NDA, price schedule, and propose onboarding date. Procurement to confirm PO and approval timeline by 2026-05-06.
